newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria hopes to revive stock market by September.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria hopes to revive stock market by September.

text.p: Bulgaria hopes to revive share trading by September with stocks of five companies trading on a joint exchange set up by the country's two biggest bourses, Deputy Industry Minister Marin Marinov said on Wednesday.
Bulgaria's Securities and Exchange Commission suspended floor trading in October after companies failed to meet legal requirements.
Marinov told Reuters he hoped the legal amendments needed to simplify share sales would be approved by the cabinet and by parliament before the assembly's summer recess in August.
Under current rules, all transfers of share ownership are handled through the Privatisation Agency.
Marinov said that to simplify the process, the government planned to permit direct sales of shares in state-owned companies to the public through the stock market.
He said transactions could bypass the Privatisation Agency if the company concerned had a prospectus approved by the Securities and Exchange Commission.

"If they have a prospectus for a public offering of shares, then there will be no need to go through the lengthy motions of Privatisation Agency assessments, legal analysis and the rest because most of those things are already included in the prospectuses," he said.

Bulgaria is overhauling its state sector under a wide-ranging reform programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, which includes pegging the lev to the mark in a currency board system from July 1.
Marinov said the Industry Ministry had a pilot programme of five companies for which it would draw up a prospectus for submission to the commission.

"We will have five profitable companies to offer immediately to the public and they will be followed by a wave of maybe 30 companies altogether to create a core of Bulgarian blue chips, so to speak, to be registered by the stock exchange so that we create a certain volume, a certain trading activity," he said.
He declined to name the companies but said they were profitable under state ownership and would be more so once in private hands.
Marinov said he hoped trading would get under way by September and Bulgaria would have a small but functioning stock market by the end of the year.

The directors of the country's two biggest exchanges, the Bulgarian Stock Exchange and the Sofia Stock Exchange, signed an agreement on June 6 to set up a joint exchange by year-end, with the proviso that if they fail, the state will set one up.
Marinov said it was now up to the two exchanges to amend their articles of association and get to work.
"The software is here, the computers are here, the people are here, the only thing that is not here is the will to overcome the differences," he said. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
